correctness.rationale: For each distinguished vertex of the cyclic three-part blow-up, the atomic out-, in-, and nonneighbor regions are determined by the part. Two remaining EF moves distinguish sizes 0, 1, >=2 in the remainder of its own part and sizes 1, >=2 in the two other parts. This proves exact pointed profiles \((\min(a,3),\min(b,2),\min(c,2))\); equal sets of pointed rank-two profiles are necessary and sufficient for three-round equivalence. The 27 truncated triples form 11 rotation orbits; direct displayed footprint substitution yields ten distinct sets with only \((2,2,3)\)/\((2,3,3)\) merging. The all-parts-at-least-three class requires nine vertices, and nine suffices. A replayed independent full-vertex signature computation and two-sided EF-game solver agree on 378 pairs at ranks 2 and 3; all 729 ordered pairs match the footprint theorem. Finite checks corroborate, not prove by extrapolation, the infinite case.

value.rationale: The family is the natural class of independent-set substitutions into the directed three-cycle. The object and invariant arise intrinsically from in-, out-, and nonneighbor regions, not an arbitrary bounded parameter slice. A complete exact classification across infinitely many sizes yields ten theories, a sharp nine-point kernel, and a structural one-off collision between cyclic necklaces \((2,2,3)\) and \((2,3,3)\) while respecting the orientation-sensitive difference between \((1,2,3)\) and \((1,3,2)\). This supplies a concrete logical profile for directed graph substitution and a reproducible model for bounded-depth distinguishing strategies, beyond a simple numerical experiment.
